entries.text: Your profile page lives under your avatar in the topbar. It is one page covering your account, your data (export + download), account deletion, and the legal record of policies you have accepted.

entries.caption: A menu opens, Profile is the one you want.
Your profile page opens, account info, your data (export), the delete-account zone, and the legal record of accepted policies.

entries.text: Before doing anything destructive, the page shows you which version of the Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, and Data Processing Addendum you accepted, and in which language. If we update any document materially we bump its version, you see "needs re-acceptance" here, and we re-prompt before any further action: so the consent record is never out of date.

entries.caption: The Legal section is the audit trail you have with markoto. Every signed-in user can read it directly, no support ticket required.

entries.text: Account deletion is irreversible after the 30-day grace window ends. So before you confirm, markoto shows exactly what will happen: which workspaces are cascade-deleted because you are the only member, which ones auto-promote a co-admin (named, so you can verify), which comments are anonymised on other people's docs, what gets retained for legal reasons. The modal makes the destructive action legible before it runs.

entries.caption: The modal lists every workspace by name and what will happen to it: deleted along with you (you are its only member), or handed to a named member who becomes admin.

entries.text: Every workspace and every new admin is named. Want to keep a workspace that would be deleted? Close the modal, invite a co-admin to it first, and come back: it moves into the "new admin" group. Nothing is lost by accident, and nobody is surprised.

The destructive button is gated behind a phrase you have to type. Same shape as GitHub repo deletion or AWS account closure: irreversible actions should never be one click away. The button stays disabled until your input matches "delete my account" exactly.
Submit: the grace banner takes over

The 30-day grace clock starts. Until it elapses, a banner sits pinned across the top of every page in markoto with a one-click cancel. The page itself flips into "scheduled for deletion" state too: same cancel button, same date. Either path restores your account exactly as it was.

entries.caption: The modal closes; the delete-account section now says your account is scheduled for deletion, with the date and a Cancel button.
Top of every page for the next 30 days: the grace banner, with the deletion date and a one-click cancel.

entries.text: Change your mind? Cancel from the banner

During the grace window you can cancel from any page, click "Cancel deletion" in the banner and the deletion request is cleared on the spot. No data lost, no collaborators surprised. Your account is back to the state it was in before the click.

entries.caption: The banner disappears and your account is back to normal, nothing was deleted.
